title: Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB) – routine data analysis
summary:
The effects of a Long or Post-COVID illness are enormous for those affected and also for their relatives. It is still not precisely known how many people are affected. Estimates suggest that 5–15% of all SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals are affected. Their care situation is, despite the existence of initial guidelines, partly highly problematic. Outpatient care providers often feel overwhelmed by the treatment. 
Through comprehensive data collection, the Innovation Fund project "Improving the care for people affected by Long/Post-COVID (LCovB)" aims to determine the prevalence of physician-diagnosed Post-COVID illness and the care situation of people affected by Long/Post-COVID, to identify gaps and barriers in care, and to derive key points for optimizing care – in particular for the outpatient care of people who are severely and persistently ill – supported by an expert panel of professionals and affected individuals. 
The overall project is divided into four study modules. 
In study module 1, the prevalence of Post-COVID illnesses and the care trajectories of affected individuals will be examined using routine data from 44 company health insurance funds. 
The results of the individual study modules will be consolidated. Based on this, recommendations for healthcare practice will be developed jointly with experts.
conditions: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome associated with COVID-19

interventions.name:
This is a non-interventional study. 
Routine data analyses will be performed of all insured individuals of the participating statutory health insurance funds with a documented Post-COVID diagnosis in the years 2021–2023 (Module 1a) and 2021–2024 (Module 1b), respectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Insured individuals from 44 participating statutory health insurances (BKK)
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals without continuous insurance coverage with a BKK fund during the observation period, individuals with a protection code (e.g., employees of BKK funds, their family members, or persons under special protection such as those in a police witness protection program), and individuals who have objected to the use of their data for research purposes.
